result.notes:
Scope: touched only the four files WP1 owns (src/alphacube/operators/common.py, src/alphacube/catalog.py, tests/test_catalog.py, tests/test_real_valued_flag.py [new]). No other file was read-modified; parser.py's unrelated pre-existing `self.daily_fields` boolean (on `_Parser`, to be renamed `self.coerce_bare_fields` in WP2) was left untouched.

New public names/signatures for later packages and reviewers:
- `operators.common.op(mode, category, arity=1, requires_window=False, pair=False, real_valued: bool = False)` -- new trailing keyword, stored in the per-name meta dict under key `"real_valued"`. Every existing call site is positional-safe (none pass more than `pair` positionally; all checked by grep).
- `catalog.STORED_DAILY_FIELDS = ("FloatCap","TotalCap","FloatShares")`, `catalog.DERIVED_DAILY_FIELDS = ("LimitWidth","BoardCode","ListAge")`, `catalog.LOG_DAILY_FIELDS = ("LogFloatCap","LogTotalCap","LogFloatShares")`, `catalog.DAILY_FIELDS` = their concatenation (9 names, defined next to `CUBE_FIELDS`). These are catalog.py's own tuples -- WP2's planned `dailyfields.py` module defines its own separately-named `STORED_FIELDS`/`DERIVED_FIELDS`/`LOG_OF` and must not import catalog.py (per the design's module boundary), so the WP2 implementer should just make sure the literal field-name strings stay in sync with these; I verified the spellings against the design doc's "The field set" section.
- `catalog.REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES: set = set()` -- mutable module-level set, a plugin's declaration channel for a kernel it does not own. Empty by default; nothing in this package adds to it.
- `Registry.__init__(self, fields, constants=CONSTANTS, daily_fields: Tuple[str,...] = ())` -- new attribute `self.daily_fields`, kept strictly parallel to (never merged with) `self.fields`. Note the asymmetric default: the bare `Registry` class defaults `daily_fields` to `()`, but `build_registry(fields=CUBE_FIELDS, daily_fields=DAILY_FIELDS)` defaults it to the full 9-name tuple -- so `default_registry().daily_fields == DAILY_FIELDS` (9 names) even though a raw `Registry(fields)` construction (if anyone ever calls it directly) still gets `()`. This matches the design doc verbatim and is pinned by tests in both files.
- `catalog._make_spec` now computes `real = bool(meta.get("real_valued", False)) or name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES`; when true it skips `_probe_distinct_values`/`_probe_constant_capable` entirely (sets `distinct=10**9, trivial=False`) rather than overriding their result. Uses `meta.get`, not `meta[...]`, so the three manual binaries (`pow`/`greater`/`less`, built from a 2-key meta dict) are unaffected.

Verified facts baked into the new tests (measured on this tree before any edit, matching the design doc's numbers exactly): `boolean_output` = 29 names, `trivial_boolean` = 22 names (listed in tests/test_real_valued_flag.py), `coarse_output` = empty, `searchable(include_boolean=False)` = 218, `searchable(include_boolean=False, include_resource_risk=False)` = 214, `len(registry) == 244` with faces `dt=121/nd=48/nt=48/shared=27` unchanged. `in_sustain_mean`/`in_sustain_stddev`/`in_sustain_product` are confirmed mis-flagged (both boolean_output and trivial_boolean today); `in_sustain` itself is correctly flagged and untouched.

Backward compatibility: no RNG stream is touched by this package at all -- `catalog.py`/`operators/common.py` never read `self._rng`; the probes each use their own locally-seeded `torch.Generator()`, unchanged. With `REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES` empty and no `@op(...)` call site passing `real_valued=True` (true after this commit), every kernel takes the exact `else` branch that existed before this change, so `boolean_output`/`trivial_boolean`/`coarse_output` are byte-identical to the pre-WP1 tree for all 244 operators -- confirmed by the exact-set pin test passing unmodified against the real registry.

Low-confidence / worth a second look: (1) placement of the design's step-6 comment ("add a comment above the probes...") -- I put it inline inside `_make_spec` directly above the new `real = bool(...)` line (which is literally above where the probes get called/skipped); a reviewer picturing a different location should feel free to move it, the content is what matters. (2) The synthetic-kernel tests in tests/test_real_valued_flag.py mutate the process-global `OPERATOR_REGISTRY` dict and `REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES` set for the duration of a single test; cleanup is via pytest fixture teardown (`try/yield/finally`) and explicit `discard`/`pop`, and I confirmed no leakage by checking the full-suite pass count is exactly baseline+10 both before and after the commit -- but any future package adding more tests that mutate these same two globals should keep the same discipline.
